column13: blurb
Honest steel. It asks nothing clever of you.
Slow, and it does not care.
Two cuts where one would do.
A long curve, and a long grudge.
Reach enough to keep the dead at arm's length.
Poise is a fiction. This is the argument.
Both ends are the business end.
It was a woodcutter's once.
Small enough to be quick with.
A wall you can carry. Your arm knows it.
You will not be moved. You will not move.
Plain, round, and enough.
Defence with an opinion.
Light enough to see what is coming.
Fire remembers what steel forgets.
Held wrong on purpose.
Grey wood, warm at the grip.
The stone hums before you do.
Someone knelt for this once.
It keeps a little of the guiding flame.
Cut, and still growing.
Wet to the touch. It should not be.
Blood takes to flame more readily than wood.
Taken from something that objected.
